subject.title: [Feature]: Telegram — full agent activity visibility (Web UI parity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off persistent Telegram activity mode, and what disclosure, redaction, retention, and message-volume policy should it use?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but implementing it changes third-party chat disclosure and retention semantics and likely adds configuration surface rather than repairing a narrow broken path.

options.title: Add guarded Telegram activity mode
options.body: Implement a default-off mode with redacted summaries, NO_REPLY/internal-turn exclusions, bounded message volume, docs, regression tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Keep current visibility model
options.body: Document progress drafts plus /verbose and /reasoning as the intended Telegram debug behavior and close this direction as not planned.

options.title: Keep detailed activity outside Telegram
options.body: Direct durable detailed activity inspection to Control UI or another observer surface and avoid retaining tool telemetry in Telegram history.

recommendation.title: Add guarded Telegram activity mode
recommendation.body: Implement a default-off mode with redacted summaries, NO_REPLY/internal-turn exclusions, bounded message volume, docs, regression tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice crosses Telegram delivery UX, Control UI parity, and security defaults, and steipete has recent adjacent UI history plus issue-timeline routing signal.
